title: OTLP -> Tempo exporter with Jaeger fallback & adaptive sampling hooks
creator: Asha Banerjee
description: Goal: Provide a robust OTLP exporter path that writes traces into Grafana Tempo for our hosted and dedicated deployments, with an automatic fallback to Jaeger-compatible endpoints for legacy dashboards. Deliverables include: 1) OTLP exporter integration in the serving runtime and gateway, 2) adaptive sampling hooks to reduce cardinality and cost, 3) configuration surface in Console for per-customer routing and sampling, and 4) e2e tests and dashboards validating latency/error trace correlation. This ticket covers engineering work to wire the exporter, add runtime flags and env vars, and verify performance in staging.
acceptance_criteria: Traces from the default hosted runtime are ingested into Tempo's OTLP collector in staging and can be queried from Grafana Traces (Tempo) for end-to-end requests
If Tempo collector is unavailable, exporter falls back to configured Jaeger HTTP endpoint without dropping traces (verified by e2e test)
Adaptive sampling plugin reduces high-cardinality attributes per policy; sampling rules configurable via Console and honored in runtime
CPU and memory overhead of tracing in p95 request path increase by <10% compared to baseline when sampling at 100%
Documentation (docs.redwood.ai/confluence link) and console feature flag exist for opt-in/out and per-customer routing
comments: 2026-02-25: Initial design review with Observability and Runtime teams. Agreed to use OTLP over gRPC with protobuf encoded traces for Tempo to align with Grafana recommended path. - Asha

2026-03-05: PM feedback (Linnea Cho): add per-customer routing UI and default sampling policies to Console; prioritize privacy-safe defaults (redact http.headers cookie/user-agent). - Linnea
2026-03-09: Security review kickoff: reviewing PII exposure and retention settings. Need explicit allowlist/denylist for span attributes. - Security

2026-03-11: CI: unit tests for exporter config parsing failing on empty endpoint env var; added fallback behavior and added tests in serving-config package. PR updated: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/897 - Diego

2026-03-12: Staging rollout alpha for two internal teams. Observability shows traces in Tempo and automated e2e asserts passed for Jaeger fallback scenario. Next: add load testing and finalize console UI. - Diego
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature flag gated PR to canary branch. 2) Deploy collector + exporter to internal staging cluster. 3) Enable for two internal services at 100% sampling and run 24h smoke + perf tests. 4) Enable adaptive sampling at 10% for public tenant group; monitor cost and errors for 7 days. 5) Gradual rollout to hosted customers with console toggle and explicit communication.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: OTLP over gRPC provides modern features and compression but requires collector availability; Jaeger HTTP fallback keeps legacy dashboards working. We must limit high-cardinality tags (user ids, full urls) and provide automatic redaction/hashed-id patterns. Consider adding an optional local relay to buffer traces during collector outages for Dedicated deployments.
